description: Fleet log line format r2 (docs/specs/fleet-logging.md). Each render case gives the structured event and the exact line both cortexkit-log (Rust) and @cortexkit/log (TS) must produce. Timestamps are fixed inputs; a renderer that reads the clock cannot pass this fixture and must accept an injected instant. Schema 2 is a breaking rewrite of schema 1: `module`+`tag` became `logger` (dotted, rooted at the module id, always followed by a colon), `session` became one entry among ordered `bound` fields rendered in a bracket before the message, and the bracket is absent when `bound` is empty. Two new sections pin the file layout: `segment_name` (the UTC day names the file) and `retention_prune` (the writer prunes by filename comparison).

cases.line: 2026-09-05T10:41:03.123Z INFO  fusiform: poll changed version=1788526509641 eras=22 facts_changed=0 arrived=2

redaction.description: The fleet default redactor applied to a complete rendered line: input -> exact output. Cases named control-* must come out unchanged; they pin the shapes the patterns must not touch.

cases.name: url-query-access-token
cases.note: a generic key=value rule misses this because https: matches as the key

cases.name: url-query-token-in-parens
cases.input: request failed for url (https://api.example.com/v1?token=abc123): connection refused
cases.output: request failed for url (https://api.example.com/v1?token=[REDACTED]): connection refused
cases.note: the value stops at ')', so the cause after the URL survives

cases.name: url-query-api-key-in-brackets
cases.note: the value stops at ']'

cases.name: query-value-with-escaped-quote-stays-balanced
cases.note: inside a quoted field a quote in the value is written \"; the value consumes backslash pairs, so the field's closing quote is never left unbalanced

parse_rejects.name: logger-without-colon
parse_rejects.note: r1 lines parse as r2 only by accident of a one-word message; the colon is what makes the logger unambiguous

parse_rejects.name: empty-bracket
parse_rejects.note: absent when nothing is bound, never []

parse_rejects.name: bracket-after-message
parse_rejects.note: context precedes the message so its column is stable; a trailing bracket is an event field value, not context

level_filter.description: CK_LOG grammar cases: spec -> whether an event at (level, logger) is emitted. A directive names a logger prefix; the most specific matching directive decides; a bare level is the root default.

cases.note: the operator's case: errors only, plus one component's metrics
a directive on a child does not raise the parent
a directive on a parent applies to every descendant
prefix match is on dotted segments, not on characters: aft does not cover aftershock
most specific wins
the aft=warn directive lowers a sibling below the root default
empty spec is the default: info
malformed spec falls back to info and reports once

segment_name.description: The active file is named by the module id and the UTC calendar day of the write. Both twins derive it from an instant; a local-time day boundary is the divergence this section exists to catch.

cases.name: engram.2026-09-05.log
cases.note: 23:59:59.999Z is still the 5th

cases.name: engram.2026-09-06.log
cases.note: 00:00:00.000Z rolls to the 6th regardless of the host's zone

cases.name: subc.2026-09-05.log
cases.note: the daemon's own log follows the same rule under run/logs/

retention_prune.description: At process start and at each day roll the writer unlinks segments older than the window, deciding by the date in the filename alone: no stat, no mtime. `today` is the UTC day of the run. A file whose name does not match <module>.<YYYY-MM-DD>.log is never touched.

cases.name: fourteen-day-window
cases.note: the boundary day (today - max_age_days = 2026-09-05) is KEPT; strictly older is unlinked; foreign names and other modules' segments are untouched

cases.name: zero-window-keeps-today
cases.note: max_age_days=0 means today only; the active segment is never a prune candidate

cases.name: malformed-date-is-not-a-segment
cases.note: a name that does not parse as a segment is left alone rather than guessed at; the pid-suffixed r1 file is one such name
